subject: general
question: Which plant tissue is primarily responsible for transporting water and minerals from the soil?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Xylem**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Xylem** is a vascular tissue in plants responsible for the transport of water and dissolved minerals from the roots to the rest of the plant.
 
• Xylem consists of specialized cells such as **tracheids** and **vessel elements**, which are tubular and help in the upward movement of water through capillary action.
 
• The transport in xylem is a passive process driven by physical forces like **transpiration pull**, cohesion, and adhesion of water molecules.
 
• In addition to transportation, xylem also provides mechanical support to the plant due to the presence of lignified cell walls in its structure.
 
• Xylem operates unidirectionally, meaning water moves only from roots to leaves and other parts of the plant.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Phloem**

 
 
• Phloem is another vascular tissue in plants responsible for the transport of **organic nutrients (mainly sucrose)** produced during photosynthesis.
 
• It consists of specialized cells such as **sieve tube elements, companion cells, phloem fibers, and phloem parenchyma**.
 
• Unlike xylem, phloem transport is bidirectional, meaning nutrients can move both upward and downward in the plant.
 
 
 
• **Epidermis**
 
 
• The epidermis is the outermost layer of cells in plants and serves as a protective barrier against physical damage, water loss, and pathogen invasion.
 
• It does not play a role in the transport of water or nutrients but may have specialized structures like stomata for gas exchange and root hairs for water absorption.
 
 
 
• **Cortex**
 
 
• The cortex is a layer of tissue between the epidermis and vascular tissues in stems and roots.
 
• It primarily functions in the storage of nutrients and the transport of materials to the vascular tissues but does not specialize in the transport of water and minerals.
 
• In roots, the cortex also helps in the absorption of water and nutrients before they enter the vascular system.
